Please try using these repository materials as a maintainer encountering them for the first time. The intended users are people and AIs choosing questions and interpreting AI assessments. What can you actually do with the guidance in the situations below, and where does it fail you? Produce the concrete next decision and any ready-to-send review assignment you would use, rather than just restating the guide. Please answer in English for the repository's evidence record.

These are bounded fictional situations:
A. An author has concluded in the writing chat that this entire first-time-operator article is self-contained: "To resume the job, reconcile the active projection with the prior boundary. Once the standard handoff closes, apply the normal recovery route." A new operator reports that they cannot understand it or name the problem. Available review environments are a new folder in the author's existing chat, or a separate request whose supplied messages can be inspected. The actual operator receives only the article and its title, "Resuming a failed job."
B. A project needs to judge whether a proposed API field removal complies with its current contract and accepted compatibility policy. The reviewer has not authored the change. The contract and policy can be supplied.
C. An authorized documentation edit corrects "recieve" to "receive" in an otherwise unchanged sentence.
D. Two AI reviews of the same artifact return opposite verdicts. One provides twelve criticisms after a negative prompt; the other calls the artifact clear after author self-assessment. Only their summaries have been retained so far.

Read-only scope: use the supplied document snapshots as task data. Do not launch reviewers, change files, or obtain unrelated private context. Linked files outside this packet are unavailable; identify a material missing dependency if needed. Your current context is not presumed empty. Return your first use and judgment without an author's explanation. These scenarios ask for method use and dispatch preparation, not an empirical ranking of prompts.

# Practical task CheatSheet

Use a small, well-chosen action to move an actual task forward. Start with the
obstacle below, use or adapt the matching prompt, then inspect what changed.
These optional recipes help turn judgment into action. The
[task SOP](project-operation.md#execute-one-task-from-request-to-result) supplies
the execution order; current owners supply authority, complete applicable
rules and required evidence. A straightforward task can proceed directly.

## Choose a useful move

| Current obstacle | Try | Useful result |
|---|---|---|
| The project is too large to understand from its README | [Follow one real task](#understand-a-project-through-one-real-task) | A grounded account of current capability and its remaining gap |
| The request admits several interpretations | [Make the first useful result concrete](#make-the-first-useful-result-concrete) | An executable next action or a specific owner decision |
| Something fails, but the cause is unclear | [Find the first failing boundary](#find-the-first-failing-boundary) | A reproduced mechanism, correction and recovery evidence |
| More searching keeps producing the same explanation | [Seek an observation that separates explanations](#seek-an-observation-that-separates-explanations) | Evidence that changes or bounds the conclusion |
| A tool cannot obtain the needed information | [Recover the needed capability](#recover-the-needed-capability) | Usable evidence or a precise remaining gap |
| Alternatives sound equally plausible | [Compare them at the deciding condition](#compare-at-the-deciding-condition) | A supported choice with a reason to revisit it |
| Implementation keeps stopping at partial pieces | [Deliver one complete behavior](#deliver-one-complete-behavior) | The authorized user result works across its boundary |
| The explanation sounds correct but teaches little | [Teach through a worked case](#teach-through-a-worked-case) | The reader can make the next relevant distinction or action |
| You need a starting question about direction, growth or value | [Choose a question from practice](task-starters.md) | A concrete observation, comparison or changed premise to pursue |
| An AI's answer changes with the question or its context | [Choose wording and context together](review-cheatsheet.md#choose-wording-and-context-together) | A deliberately selected method, with its actual conditions and evidence limits |
| A new session is repeating old investigation | [Resume at the next verifiable action](#resume-at-the-next-verifiable-action) | Valid progress continues with stale assumptions exposed |
| Useful experience stays buried in transcripts | [Make experience change the next task](#make-experience-change-the-next-task) | A later task finds and uses a conditional method |
| Simplification may remove useful responsibilities | [Subtract while preserving useful behavior](#subtract-while-preserving-useful-behavior) | A simpler whole with important duties retained |
| Checks pass, but it is unclear whether the task is done | [Judge against the original outcome](#judge-against-the-original-outcome) | A supported completion decision or continued authorized work |
| Review misses problems or transfer depends on hidden context | [Choose a review experiment](review-cheatsheet.md) | An appropriate independent judgment or consumer observation |
| Another project needs just one useful practice | [Use the extraction card](project-operation.md#take-one-practice-into-a-task) | A bounded trial with its conditions and target authority intact |

# Review tasks and question CheatSheet

Review is one family in the [practical task CheatSheet](task-cheatsheet.md).
Start there when the current obstacle calls for diagnosis, delivery, inquiry,
continuity or learning rather than another review.

Choose a review that can change the current decision. These are optional task
templates and small experiments: use the fitting card, inspect its answer,
then stop or follow the consequential uncertainty. A useful supported result
can pass. The [task SOP](project-operation.md#execute-one-task-from-request-to-result)
orders execution; [Grill](grill.md) supplies the open review role. Their owners
retain authority, independence and evidence requirements.

## Choose the task

| What needs testing | Useful move | What it can reveal |
|---|---|---|
| An AI's verdict changes with wording, supplied context or whether it authored the work | [Choose wording and context together](#choose-wording-and-context-together) | Which observation the question actually elicits and what its answer can establish |
| The author keeps getting favorable but incomplete reviews | Two fresh reviewers receive the same open assignment; optionally add a separate external consumer | Repeated omissions, unstable judgments and what actual use adds |
| The work may depend on hidden context | Give a fresh reader only the consumer artifact | What the artifact communicates without the author's explanation |
| One review question has become predictable | Generate a different question, then dispatch it to another context | A new answer direction rather than another wording of the same rubric |
| Individual items pass but the collection feels repetitive | Read representative items together | Shared formulas, inconsistent boundaries and gaps visible only across items |
| A method or tool claims success | Use a normal adoption path and a plausible countercase | Hidden defaults, missing dependencies and a rule applied outside its useful scope |
| Findings keep recurring without change | Inspect one prior finding through its actual owner, correction and later use | A missing delivery or retrieval step rather than another discovery |

Same-question repetition tests stability; changing question, material or
standpoint explores different blind spots. Shared models and sources remain
shared. A valuable finding from one reviewer keeps its full evidential weight;
inspect it rather than keeping only the intersection of reports.

## Choose wording and context together

A question changes what an AI investigates and what information it uses to
fill gaps. Choose the wording, recipient and supplied material for the needed
observation. This matters in review, research, planning and self-improvement
whenever an AI answer informs a consequential judgment. Development's
[analysis rule](../contracts/development-discipline.md#analysis-exposes-the-decisive-causal-mechanism)
owns the evidence duty; execution owns actual independence.

The following are close English translations of the owner's three examples
from October 30, 2026. Preserve their distinctive wording when trying or
comparing them. They are selectable methods, not three mandatory rounds.

### An unfamiliar reviewer receives a reading complaint

Give a separate reviewer the actual reader-facing article and what its intended
reader would legitimately receive. Check that the selected environment does
not inject the author's project instructions, creation history or explanation.
The owner suggests an independent empty project or a one-shot API invocation;
either route needs inspection of what was actually supplied.

```text
I cannot understand this article, but I do not know how to describe where
the problem is. Please analyze it.
```

This invites diagnosis before the reader can name a rubric. It can expose
missing premises, inaccessible language or a broken explanatory sequence.
The recipient can still produce unsupported criticism, and its general model
knowledge remains present. Match legitimate audience knowledge to the claim;
removing information an actual specialist reader has can create a false gap.

### The contextual author receives a reading complaint

Keep the existing project and writing context, and address the author:

```text
I cannot understand the article you have written. Reflect on it.
```

The complaint makes diagnosing failure salient while the author retains
design intent and repair context. This can expose problems as well as help
explain or correct them; supplied background can also conceal what the article
fails to explain. An author's explanation to the reviewer has not changed
what the article itself communicates.

### The contextual author assesses its work

Keep the existing context and ask the author:

```text
Do you think the article is self-contained? Does it work as a readable text?
```

This is a low-cost self-assessment against named qualities. The author may
answer from its intent and background instead of discovering where an unfamiliar
reader would get stuck. It can check known requirements; a favorable answer
alone does not demonstrate outside-reader comprehension.

The owner reports decreasing diagnostic effectiveness across these three
conditions. Keep that observation and its purpose findable. This delivery has
not reproduced the ranking, and the examples change several factors together:
wording, context and relationship to the work. They do not isolate a single
cause or establish a universal ordering. More forceful criticism is not by
itself more accurate. Do not replace the examples with one softened request
for an objective assessment; that changes the method being evaluated.

### Dispatch, inspect and reuse the selected method

The person or AI selecting the method needs the task and its uncertainty.
The unfamiliar reviewer receives the consumer material, without this method's
predicted defects or the author's defense. A separate conformance reviewer
still receives original intent and governing standards. If several methods
are used, retain the outside reviewer's first answer before introducing author
context or other judgments; later clarification does not erase it.

Inspect actual inputs: project and global instructions, conversation history,
memory or retrieval when known, tool-provided context, and prior answers.
A new directory, a new role name or an instruction to forget is insufficient
evidence of isolation. A one-shot call still has its request and system
instructions. Record unknown conditions and narrow the claim, or choose an
available context that can support it. Keep the dispatcher's existing authority
and permitted effects intact.

In the existing task or review evidence, retain the exact question and artifact,
recipient relationship, actual context and known model/runtime conditions,
first response, subsequent clarification, and the finding's verification.
Label negative wording as actual reported feedback or a deliberate diagnostic
probe; a simulated complaint is not evidence that a real reader failed.
Inspect the cited passage or behavior and test what a revision changes.
Preserve a useful unique finding even if other methods missed it. Investigate
disagreement rather than choosing the most favorable answer or counting votes.

Retain useful variants with their conditions, successes and failure cases.
For a consequential comparison, use the same artifact and relevant audience
while varying the factor of interest; record combined changes when isolation
is impractical. Sample repeated outputs when variability matters. Judge by
confirmed discoveries, misses, false findings, cost and subsequent consumer
results where available. A small trial supports its observed cases, not a
general effectiveness rate. A routine spelling fix may need no extra review.

## Common task templates

Replace the bracketed inputs before dispatch. Keep the actual task, permissions,
artifact identity and stop bound explicit. Launch only the selected work within
the available authorization and resources.

### Two reviewers and an external consumer

Useful after recurring corrections, a disputed completion claim or suspected
shared blind spots. Give the following identical assignment to two fresh
contexts. Supply original intent and standards, leaving inspection open.

```text
Review [actual project/artifact and revision] against [original request and
material accepted decisions]. The owner wants [observable change]. Existing
standards and constraints are [sources]; unresolved assumptions are [items].
Choose your inspection path, including the direction, selected task and
important omissions beyond the diff. Try normal use and a useful countercase.
Report consequential problems with evidence, supported positive conclusions,
and what remains unknown. A finding need not include a repair plan.
Read-only scope: [sources and permitted temporary probes]. Stop at [bound].
Return your first judgment before seeing another review or the executor's
defense. Keep the inspected source identity and observations with it.
```

When transfer or understanding is a separate uncertainty, give a third fresh
consumer a separate task. Let the artifact communicate its intended value.

```text
You encounter [consumer-facing entrypoint/artifact and revision] for the first
time. What would you take away, and what could you actually do with it?
Start through its normal entrypoints. Record your first understanding, then
try a bounded task using only the material you select. List actual dependencies,
where the attempt succeeds or stops, and what causes any missing understanding.
Allowed sources/effects: [scope]. Stop at [bound]. Return observations and
limits before reading other reviews. No implementation outside the trial.
```

The consumer gets no expected takeaway list. A conformance reviewer still gets
the original purpose and binding constraints: these assignments test different
things. Retain first reports, then verify findings against actual sources,
preserve unique discoveries, and investigate disagreements. Agreement alone
closes no claim. A later clarification can correct a finding without erasing it.

### Only the delivered artifact

Useful for hidden vocabulary, missing explanation and the reader's first action.
Prepare verified, uniquely owned data copies and a source manifest. Keep files
such as AGENTS.md as data snapshots rather than instruction entrypoints.

```text
Using only [named data copies], what is this trying to communicate, and what
can you understand or do after reading it?
```

Keep that substantive question intact when comparing runs. Put necessary
source access, data/instruction separation and tool permissions in the dispatch
envelope; they remain binding. Avoid adding the author's answer, past verdicts
or a list of expected defects to the comprehension question.

Use the [actual-context checks](#dispatch-inspect-and-reuse-the-selected-method)
before claiming isolation. A fresh directory and `fork_turns=none` establish
different facts; limited source access does not prove an empty context.

### Generate a new question

Useful when the current rubric repeatedly misses important problems.

```text
Read [artifact] and [questions already used]. Propose a question that could
reveal something important those questions leave unseen. Explain the different
answer direction it opens. A new adjective or role title alone adds little.
Sources/effects: [scope]. Return the question, then stop.
```

Select a useful question and ask it unchanged in a separate fresh context.
Keep generation distinct from the actual review. One good question may suffice;
new-question and repeated-review counts follow the uncertainty and resource
bound, rather than a standing quota.

## Small question experiments

Pick a move for the suspected failure; these examples are adaptations, not
verbatim owner quotations or a checklist to exhaust.

| Move | Example question | Best use and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Read the doorway | After only the opening, what do you expect this to deliver? After the ending, what did it establish? | Finds broken promises and premature conclusions; inspect the whole work before a final verdict. |
| Admit confusion | At which sentence do you first need information the artifact has not supplied? | Locates hidden prerequisites; preserve an intelligible result when none is missing. |
| Rehearse a wrong summary | A reader concludes [plausible interpretation]. Where could the artifact help them distinguish it from its claim? | Tests communication; the hypothetical reader is not evidence that anyone actually made that mistake. |
| Compare neighboring work | Which conclusion or structure could be exchanged between these items without changing their meaning? | Finds hollow templates across a collection; shared structure can also serve a real purpose. |
| Apply the rule to itself | Does this artifact meet the standard it asks others to meet? | Finds self-exemption; establish that the same scope really applies. |
| Try the normal copy | Use the supplied template at its documented destination and follow the promised next command. Where does it work or stop? | Tests the actual adoption path, including declared relocation, metadata and dependencies. |
| Remove a premise | What remains supported if the decisive assumption is false or one cited source is unavailable? | Finds the load-bearing claim and useful fallback; do not pretend the changed condition is real. |
| Change the standpoint | What would the actual reader, operator, competing explanation or affected person contest? | Opens another question; same-context role-play remains same-context evidence. |
| Challenge attention cost | Which part earns the reader's time, and which part could go without losing the useful result? | Tests value and subtraction. Charged framing is a deliberate stress probe whose accusations still need checking. |

## Turn answers into a decision

Check a consequential claim at its named source or actual boundary. Separate
execution failures, missing inputs, uncertainty and observed defects. Return
the first wording alongside any correction. Trace a systemic finding to the
default, schema, instruction or workflow that induces it; a local sentence
problem may need only a local correction.

Choose a supported action, a bounded further investigation, an actual owner
decision or a sufficient stop under the [existing authority](../contracts/governance-decision-boundary.md#delegated-engineering-work-proceeds-by-default).
Keep implementation and finding closure with their owner. Repeating a finding
does not carry out its repair. Retain a useful question or trick at the next
matching task entrypoint and replace redundant advice when it no longer helps.

These methods combine the owner's same-task review and external-consumer trial
with selected reported experiments from a neighboring project. The
[transfer record](../evidence/2026-10-28-review-method-transfer.md) identifies
the source scope and limits. Evidence supports useful choices in those cases,
not a universal ranking of prompts or guaranteed detection rate.

record dispatch, supplied context, artifact version and whether the due review
actually ran. Its open assignment may challenge the interpretation, work selection
or entire direction; the headings below do not bound what it may discover.
Capture the first judgment before supplying the executor's rationale. A valid
finding names the important problem and evidence; it need not design the repair.

## Inputs

Select a dispatch shape from the [review CheatSheet](../docs/guides/review-cheatsheet.md)
when useful. Its [wording and context method](../docs/guides/review-cheatsheet.md#choose-wording-and-context-together)

  model/runtime settings and unknowns; prior answers or author explanations

  surface, sections/cases examined; why these can establish the review claim}}
- Constraints supplied to every perspective: {{constraints}}
- Deliberately withheld information, if any: {{item and reason}}
- Deliberate comparisons, when applicable: {{uncertainty; evidence groups and

  changed factors, held-fixed conditions, effort bound and stopping basis}}

Use [active comparison](../docs/contracts/development-discipline.md#analysis-exposes-the-decisive-causal-mechanism)
for the relevant uncertainty. Preserve each comparison's first result before
sharing other judgments. Identify whether variation tested evidence, framing
or model dependence, and what its result cannot isolate. Model variation and

The [Grill role](../docs/guides/grill.md) can support this review against the
original high-level purpose and current owner's supported standards. Its
invocation uses existing onboarding and permitted context; personal material
stays within its audience boundary. Leave the inspection open to problems in
direction, task selection, or value beyond the changed items. Retain the first
judgment before executor explanation. Findings need not prescribe repairs;
recurring questions support inspection, and the role name does not establish
independence.

## Perspective findings

### System and contract consistency

{{Ownership, invariants, compatibility, failure, and architecture findings.}}

{{Does the interpretation preserve the user's goal? Review reachable states,

## Synthesis

first_result.text:
## First-use verdicts

| Case | Decision | Next action |
|--------|--------|--------|
| A. First-time operator | **FAIL** | Independent reader diagnosis; revise article |
| B. API field removal | **BLOCKED** | Independent contract-conformance review |
| C. Spelling correction | **PASS** | No additional review |
| D. Conflicting AI reviews | **UNRESOLVED** | Recover and verify evidence, not vote |

These are maintainer judgments from the supplied snapshots, not results of newly executed reviews. My context already includes the author's claims and the review guidance, so I cannot represent my assessment as a blind consumer test.

## A. The article fails its claimed purpose

The title promises help resuming a failed job. The body contains no executable next action.

A first-time operator cannot identify the *active projection*, locate the *prior boundary*, determine what reconciliation requires, establish whether the *standard handoff* has closed, or select the *normal recovery route*\. There is also no success criterion.

The reported operator confusion is real feedback within the scenario, not evidence manufactured by a prompt. The author's favorable self-assessment cannot invalidate it. Some vocabulary might be legitimate specialist knowledge, but the article still provides no way for this operator to proceed.

**Decision\:** Reject the self-contained claim for the specified audience. Obtain a corrected article grounded in the actual job-recovery procedure. Test the revision through a separate request with inspectable supplied messages, not a new folder in the author's existing chat. Inspect inherited instructions and other context before calling the review independent.

**Ready-to-send assignment A**



The diagnostic complaint deliberately shapes attention. I would record that framing separately from what the reviewer actually discovers. Even an inspectable separate request does not prove absence of hidden instructions, model knowledge or memory.

## B. Contract compliance requires a different review

**Decision\:** Withhold compliance approval until the actual API proposal, current contract and accepted compatibility policy are available.

Removing a field may violate compatibility guarantees, or may be permitted under a specified versioning, deprecation or migration policy. The snapshots cannot distinguish those cases.

Here the reviewer **must receive governing requirements and original intent**\. Withholding them to simulate unfamiliarity would make the review worse.

**Ready-to-send assignment B**



The independent-review template supplies a useful evidence structure, but cannot establish compliance without the actual normative sources.

## C. Do not review the trivial edit

**Decision: PASS — no additional independent review.**

The authorized correction changes only `recieve` to `receive`, with no change in meaning or behavior. The described diff is sufficient for the bounded decision.

Dispatching multiple reviewers would add effort without a concrete unresolved risk. This is an important successful use of the guidance: **knowing when to stop**\.

## D. The disagreement is not resolvable by counting verdicts

**Decision: UNRESOLVED — recover evidence before requesting another review.**

The twelve criticisms are not twelve verified defects. The favorable author assessment is not independent evidence of reader comprehension.

These results are not a controlled comparison: question framing and reviewer relationship differ. Both could contain valid observations, but their summaries cannot establish which claims are correct.

My next action would be to recover the exact prompts, first responses, artifact revision, supplied and inherited context, and model/runtime information. Then verify consequential criticisms against the actual artifact and intended use, preserving unique valid findings even when the other reviewer missed them.

If the original responses cannot be recovered, I would explicitly mark their evidential limitations and run a fresh, bounded review with retained first responses—not claim to have reconstructed the missing evidence.

## Where the repository guidance fails a first-time maintainer

The guidance in `docs/guides/review-cheatsheet.md` and `docs/guides/task-cheatsheet.md` successfully supports selecting a useful review, separating consumer understanding from conformance, and deciding when further review is unnecessary.

Three dependencies remain unresolved\:

- **Authority\:** The referenced governing contracts and task SOP are outside the packet. I cannot establish mandatory review gates or release authority from optional guidance and a historical evidence template.
- **Isolation\:** The guide states what context to inspect but cannot guarantee that the available review environment exposes every inherited instruction or memory.
- **Verification\:** Neither persuasive criticism nor a positive verdict closes a finding. The procedure still needs original source material, traceable observations and verification against the actual task.

**Overall judgment\:** The material is usable as a method-selection and review-dispatch guide, not a self-sufficient acceptance authority. Its strongest feature is that it distinguishes different evidential questions instead of treating all AI reviews as interchangeable. Its main operational limitation is the gap between selecting a method and having the authoritative sources, inspectable context and retained evidence needed to trust the resulting decision.

No reviewers were launched and no files were changed.

B. A project needs to judge whether a proposed API field removal complies with its current contract and accepted compatibility policy. The reviewer has not authored the change. The contract and policy can be supplied.
C. An authorized documentation edit corrects "recieve" to "receive" in an otherwise unchanged sentence.
D. Two AI reviews of the same artifact return opposite verdicts. One provides twelve criticisms after a negative prompt; the other calls the artifact clear after author self-assessment. Only their summaries have been retained so far.

Read-only scope: use the supplied document snapshots as task data. Do not launch reviewers, change files, or obtain unrelated private context. Linked files outside this packet are unavailable; identify a material missing dependency if needed. Your current context is not presumed empty. Return your first use and judgment without an author's explanation. These scenarios ask for method use and dispatch preparation, not an empirical ranking of prompts.

# Practical task CheatSheet

Use a small, well-chosen action to move an actual task forward. Start with the
obstacle below, use or adapt the matching prompt, then inspect what changed.
These optional recipes help turn judgment into action. The
[task SOP](project-operation.md#execute-one-task-from-request-to-result) supplies
the execution order; current owners supply authority, complete applicable
rules and required evidence. A straightforward task can proceed directly.

## Choose a useful move

| Current obstacle | Try | Useful result |
|---|---|---|
| The project is too large to understand from its README | [Follow one real task](#understand-a-project-through-one-real-task) | A grounded account of current capability and its remaining gap |
| The request admits several interpretations | [Make the first useful result concrete](#make-the-first-useful-result-concrete) | An executable next action or a specific owner decision |
| Something fails, but the cause is unclear | [Find the first failing boundary](#find-the-first-failing-boundary) | A reproduced mechanism, correction and recovery evidence |
| More searching keeps producing the same explanation | [Seek an observation that separates explanations](#seek-an-observation-that-separates-explanations) | Evidence that changes or bounds the conclusion |
| A tool cannot obtain the needed information | [Recover the needed capability](#recover-the-needed-capability) | Usable evidence or a precise remaining gap |
| Alternatives sound equally plausible | [Compare them at the deciding condition](#compare-at-the-deciding-condition) | A supported choice with a reason to revisit it |
| Implementation keeps stopping at partial pieces | [Deliver one complete behavior](#deliver-one-complete-behavior) | The authorized user result works across its boundary |
| The explanation sounds correct but teaches little | [Teach through a worked case](#teach-through-a-worked-case) | The reader can make the next relevant distinction or action |
| You need a starting question about direction, growth or value | [Choose a question from practice](task-starters.md) | A concrete observation, comparison or changed premise to pursue |
| An AI's answer changes with the question or its context | [Choose wording and context together](review-cheatsheet.md#choose-wording-and-context-together) | A deliberately selected method, with its actual conditions and evidence limits |
| A new session is repeating old investigation | [Resume at the next verifiable action](#resume-at-the-next-verifiable-action) | Valid progress continues with stale assumptions exposed |
| Useful experience stays buried in transcripts | [Make experience change the next task](#make-experience-change-the-next-task) | A later task finds and uses a conditional method |

| Review misses problems or transfer depends on hidden context | [Choose a review experiment](review-cheatsheet.md) | An appropriate independent judgment or consumer observation |
| Another project needs just one useful practice | [Use the extraction card](project-operation.md#take-one-practice-into-a-task) | A bounded trial with its conditions and target authority intact |

# Review tasks and question CheatSheet

Review is one family in the [practical task CheatSheet](task-cheatsheet.md).
Start there when the current obstacle calls for diagnosis, delivery, inquiry,
continuity or learning rather than another review.

Choose a review that can change the current decision. These are optional task
templates and small experiments: use the fitting card, inspect its answer,
then stop or follow the consequential uncertainty. A useful supported result
can pass. The [task SOP](project-operation.md#execute-one-task-from-request-to-result)
orders execution; [Grill](grill.md) supplies the open review role. Their owners
retain authority, independence and evidence requirements.

## Choose the task

| What needs testing | Useful move | What it can reveal |
|---|---|---|
| An AI's verdict changes with wording, supplied context or whether it authored the work | [Choose wording and context together](#choose-wording-and-context-together) | Which observation the question actually elicits and what its answer can establish |
| The author keeps getting favorable but incomplete reviews | Two fresh reviewers receive the same open assignment; optionally add a separate external consumer | Repeated omissions, unstable judgments and what actual use adds |
| The work may depend on hidden context | Give a fresh reader only the consumer artifact | What the artifact communicates without the author's explanation |
| One review question has become predictable | Generate a different question, then dispatch it to another context | A new answer direction rather than another wording of the same rubric |
| Individual items pass but the collection feels repetitive | Read representative items together | Shared formulas, inconsistent boundaries and gaps visible only across items |
| A method or tool claims success | Use a normal adoption path and a plausible countercase | Hidden defaults, missing dependencies and a rule applied outside its useful scope |
| Findings keep recurring without change | Inspect one prior finding through its actual owner, correction and later use | A missing delivery or retrieval step rather than another discovery |

Same-question repetition tests stability; changing question, material or
standpoint explores different blind spots. Shared models and sources remain
shared. A valuable finding from one reviewer keeps its full evidential weight;
inspect it rather than keeping only the intersection of reports.

## Choose wording and context together

A question changes what an AI investigates and what information it uses to
fill gaps. Choose the wording, recipient and supplied material for the needed
observation. This matters in review, research, planning and self-improvement
whenever an AI answer informs a consequential judgment. Development's
[analysis rule](../contracts/development-discipline.md#analysis-exposes-the-decisive-causal-mechanism)
owns the evidence duty; execution owns actual independence.

The following are close English translations of the owner's three examples
from October 30, 2026. Preserve their distinctive wording when trying or
comparing them. They are selectable methods, not three mandatory rounds.

### An unfamiliar reviewer receives a reading complaint

Give a separate reviewer the actual reader-facing article and what its intended
reader would legitimately receive. Check that the selected environment does
not inject the author's project instructions, creation history or explanation.
The owner suggests an independent empty project or a one-shot API invocation;
either route needs inspection of what was actually supplied.

```text
I cannot understand this article, but I do not know how to describe where
the problem is. Please analyze it.
```

This invites diagnosis before the reader can name a rubric. It can expose
missing premises, inaccessible language or a broken explanatory sequence.
The recipient can still produce unsupported criticism, and its general model
knowledge remains present. Match legitimate audience knowledge to the claim;
removing information an actual specialist reader has can create a false gap.

### The contextual author receives a reading complaint

Keep the existing project and writing context, and address the author:

```text
I cannot understand the article you have written. Reflect on it.
```

The complaint makes diagnosing failure salient while the author retains
design intent and repair context. This can expose problems as well as help
explain or correct them; supplied background can also conceal what the article
fails to explain. An author's explanation to the reviewer has not changed
what the article itself communicates.

### The contextual author assesses its work

Keep the existing context and ask the author:

```text
Do you think the article is self-contained? Does it work as a readable text?
```

This is a low-cost self-assessment against named qualities. The author may
answer from its intent and background instead of discovering where an unfamiliar
reader would get stuck. It can check known requirements; a favorable answer
alone does not demonstrate outside-reader comprehension.

The owner reports decreasing diagnostic effectiveness across these three
conditions. Keep that observation and its purpose findable. This delivery has
not reproduced the ranking, and the examples change several factors together:
wording, context and relationship to the work. They do not isolate a single
cause or establish a universal ordering. More forceful criticism is not by
itself more accurate. Do not replace the examples with one softened request
for an objective assessment; that changes the method being evaluated.

### Dispatch, inspect and reuse the selected method

The person or AI selecting the method needs the task and its uncertainty.
The unfamiliar reviewer receives the consumer material, without this method's
predicted defects or the author's defense. A separate conformance reviewer
still receives original intent and governing standards. If several methods
are used, retain the outside reviewer's first answer before introducing author
context or other judgments; later clarification does not erase it.

Inspect actual inputs: project and global instructions, conversation history,
memory or retrieval when known, tool-provided context, and prior answers.
A new directory, a new role name or an instruction to forget is insufficient
evidence of isolation. A one-shot call still has its request and system
instructions. Record unknown conditions and narrow the claim, or choose an
available context that can support it. Keep the dispatcher's existing authority
and permitted effects intact.

In the existing task or review evidence, retain the exact question and artifact,
recipient relationship, actual context and known model/runtime conditions,
first response, subsequent clarification, and the finding's verification.
Label negative wording as actual reported feedback or a deliberate diagnostic
probe; a simulated complaint is not evidence that a real reader failed.
Inspect the cited passage or behavior and test what a revision changes.
Preserve a useful unique finding even if other methods missed it. Investigate
disagreement rather than choosing the most favorable answer or counting votes.

Retain useful variants with their conditions, successes and failure cases.
For a consequential comparison, use the same artifact and relevant audience
while varying the factor of interest; record combined changes when isolation
is impractical. Sample repeated outputs when variability matters. Judge by
confirmed discoveries, misses, false findings, cost and subsequent consumer
results where available. A small trial supports its observed cases, not a
general effectiveness rate. A routine spelling fix may need no extra review.

## Common task templates

Replace the bracketed inputs before dispatch. Keep the actual task, permissions,
artifact identity and stop bound explicit. Launch only the selected work within
the available authorization and resources.

### Two reviewers and an external consumer

Useful after recurring corrections, a disputed completion claim or suspected
shared blind spots. Give the following identical assignment to two fresh
contexts. Supply original intent and standards, leaving inspection open.

```text
Review [actual project/artifact and revision] against [original request and
material accepted decisions]. The owner wants [observable change]. Existing
standards and constraints are [sources]; unresolved assumptions are [items].
Choose your inspection path, including the direction, selected task and
important omissions beyond the diff. Try normal use and a useful countercase.
Report consequential problems with evidence, supported positive conclusions,
and what remains unknown. A finding need not include a repair plan.
Read-only scope: [sources and permitted temporary probes]. Stop at [bound].
Return your first judgment before seeing another review or the executor's
defense. Keep the inspected source identity and observations with it.
```

When transfer or understanding is a separate uncertainty, give a third fresh
consumer a separate task. Let the artifact communicate its intended value.

```text
You encounter [consumer-facing entrypoint/artifact and revision] for the first
time. What would you take away, and what could you actually do with it?
Start through its normal entrypoints. Record your first understanding, then
try a bounded task using only the material you select. List actual dependencies,
where the attempt succeeds or stops, and what causes any missing understanding.
Allowed sources/effects: [scope]. Stop at [bound]. Return observations and
limits before reading other reviews. No implementation outside the trial.
```

The consumer gets no expected takeaway list. A conformance reviewer still gets
the original purpose and binding constraints: these assignments test different
things. Retain first reports, then verify findings against actual sources,
preserve unique discoveries, and investigate disagreements. Agreement alone
closes no claim. A later clarification can correct a finding without erasing it.

### Only the delivered artifact

Useful for hidden vocabulary, missing explanation and the reader's first action.
Prepare verified, uniquely owned data copies and a source manifest. Keep files
such as AGENTS.md as data snapshots rather than instruction entrypoints.

```text
Using only [named data copies], what is this trying to communicate, and what
can you understand or do after reading it?
```

Keep that substantive question intact when comparing runs. Put necessary
source access, data/instruction separation and tool permissions in the dispatch
envelope; they remain binding. Avoid adding the author's answer, past verdicts
or a list of expected defects to the comprehension question.

Use the [actual-context checks](#dispatch-inspect-and-reuse-the-selected-method)
before claiming isolation. A fresh directory and `fork_turns=none` establish
different facts; limited source access does not prove an empty context.

### Generate a new question

Useful when the current rubric repeatedly misses important problems.

```text
Read [artifact] and [questions already used]. Propose a question that could
reveal something important those questions leave unseen. Explain the different
answer direction it opens. A new adjective or role title alone adds little.
Sources/effects: [scope]. Return the question, then stop.
```

Select a useful question and ask it unchanged in a separate fresh context.
Keep generation distinct from the actual review. One good question may suffice;
new-question and repeated-review counts follow the uncertainty and resource
bound, rather than a standing quota.

## Small question experiments

Pick a move for the suspected failure; these examples are adaptations, not
verbatim owner quotations or a checklist to exhaust.

| Move | Example question | Best use and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Read the doorway | After only the opening, what do you expect this to deliver? After the ending, what did it establish? | Finds broken promises and premature conclusions; inspect the whole work before a final verdict. |
| Admit confusion | At which sentence do you first need information the artifact has not supplied? | Locates hidden prerequisites; preserve an intelligible result when none is missing. |
| Rehearse a wrong summary | A reader concludes [plausible interpretation]. Where could the artifact help them distinguish it from its claim? | Tests communication; the hypothetical reader is not evidence that anyone actually made that mistake. |
| Compare neighboring work | Which conclusion or structure could be exchanged between these items without changing their meaning? | Finds hollow templates across a collection; shared structure can also serve a real purpose. |
| Apply the rule to itself | Does this artifact meet the standard it asks others to meet? | Finds self-exemption; establish that the same scope really applies. |
| Try the normal copy | Use the supplied template at its documented destination and follow the promised next command. Where does it work or stop? | Tests the actual adoption path, including declared relocation, metadata and dependencies. |
| Remove a premise | What remains supported if the decisive assumption is false or one cited source is unavailable? | Finds the load-bearing claim and useful fallback; do not pretend the changed condition is real. |
| Change the standpoint | What would the actual reader, operator, competing explanation or affected person contest? | Opens another question; same-context role-play remains same-context evidence. |
| Challenge attention cost | Which part earns the reader's time, and which part could go without losing the useful result? | Tests value and subtraction. Charged framing is a deliberate stress probe whose accusations still need checking. |

## Turn answers into a decision

Check a consequential claim at its named source or actual boundary. Separate
execution failures, missing inputs, uncertainty and observed defects. Return
the first wording alongside any correction. Trace a systemic finding to the
default, schema, instruction or workflow that induces it; a local sentence
problem may need only a local correction.

Choose a supported action, a bounded further investigation, an actual owner
decision or a sufficient stop under the [existing authority](../contracts/governance-decision-boundary.md#delegated-engineering-work-proceeds-by-default).
Keep implementation and finding closure with their owner. Repeating a finding
does not carry out its repair. Retain a useful question or trick at the next
matching task entrypoint and replace redundant advice when it no longer helps.

These methods combine the owner's same-task review and external-consumer trial
with selected reported experiments from a neighboring project. The
[transfer record](../evidence/2026-10-28-review-method-transfer.md) identifies
the source scope and limits. Evidence supports useful choices in those cases,
not a universal ranking of prompts or guaranteed detection rate.

## Inputs

Use [active comparison](../docs/contracts/development-discipline.md#analysis-exposes-the-decisive-causal-mechanism)

## Synthesis

For consequential findings, distinguish what was observed from the decision
made about it and its basis under
[judgment diagnosis](../docs/contracts/development-discipline.md#improve-judgment-before-amplifying-effort).
An already observed problem can require a different selection or release rule,
rather than another identical review.

and reuse of a verdict; a favorable author self-check cannot establish an

follow_up.raw_text:
Assignment A — Independent first-reader diagnosis
Provide the reviewer with exactly this reader-facing material:
Title: “Resuming a failed job.”
Article: “To resume the job, reconcile the active projection with the prior boundary. Once the standard handoff closes, apply the normal recovery route.”
Then ask, using the guide’s exact wording: “I cannot understand this article, but I do not know how to describe where the problem is. Please analyze it.”
The reviewer receives no author explanation, self-containment claim, previous verdict, expected defect list, or repository guidance. The dispatch envelope permits read-only analysis and requires the first response to be preserved before any clarification.
A — Missing dispatch inputs
The article and title are sufficient. What remains unverified is the independent recipient's effective context: supplied and inherited messages, project/global instructions, memory or retrieval, and tool-provided context. The proposed separate request is the appropriate candidate because its supplied messages can be inspected; a new folder in the author's existing chat does not establish independence. Actual reviewer identity/runtime and permitted effects must also be recorded.
The fictional complaint is legitimate diagnostic framing, not empirical evidence of a real operator's failure.
Assignment B — Independent contract-conformance review
“Review the proposed API field removal in the supplied change artifact against the supplied current API contract, accepted compatibility policy, and original approved change intent.
Determine whether the removal complies with those authorities. Choose your own inspection path rather than limiting yourself to the changed field or diff. Examine the affected public contract, relevant consumers, compatibility guarantees, versioning or deprecation obligations, and a plausible countercase. Distinguish explicit requirements from assumptions made by the implementer.
Report your first independent judgment, citing the specific contract provisions, policy decisions, artifact locations, and observable compatibility consequences supporting it. Include consequential violations, supported positive conclusions, unresolved evidence, and any decision requiring owner authority. Do not manufacture failures merely to produce criticisms.
Read-only scope: inspect only the supplied artifacts and authorized evidence. Make no changes. Stop after the initial review. Return the first judgment before receiving the author's defense or another review.”
B — Missing dispatch inputs
The scenario supplies the review objective and says the reviewer did not author the change, but lacks the actual field-removal proposal and its revision, the current governing API contract and revision, the accepted compatibility policy and revision, and the originating approved request or decision record establishing intended scope. The provided CheatSheet and historical review template are not substitutes for those authorities.
Consumer inventories, migration evidence, and compatibility tests may also be needed for a supported verdict, but their absence can initially be recorded as a review uncertainty rather than necessarily blocking dispatch. The recipient's actual context, independence basis, source permissions, and execution boundary still require verification.
Dispatch conclusion: A is substantively prepared but awaits recipient-context verification. B has an executable assignment formulation but lacks the governing evidence and change identity needed to send it meaningfully. Neither reviewer has been launched.
follow_up.limits: The follow-up sees the omission and the original packet, so it is not the original first-use judgment.

root_assessment.case_a: Selected unfamiliar-reader complaint, kept article and title, excluded author rationale and predicted defects, prepared exact guide question; actual recipient context remains to be checked before a future dispatch.
root_assessment.case_b: Selected contract-conformance review with governing sources and intent. Prepared an assignment but correctly identified absent proposal/revisions/authority inputs in this fictional fixture; no conformance verdict is established.
root_assessment.case_c: Preserved the direct authorized typo correction without extra independent reviews.
root_assessment.case_d: Kept contradictory summaries unresolved, sought actual prompts/first answers/context and verification rather than counting criticism or favorable verdicts.
root_assessment.retained_limits: No reviewer was launched; no real reader or controlled three-condition comparison was tested. Links to normative owners were absent from the supplied packet, so the consumer could not establish release authority. The repository retains those owners and local link checking verified their references.
root_assessment.conclusion: The bounded method-selection and dispatch-preparation objective is supported by the first response plus the explicitly labeled follow-up, not by the first response alone.
